name: Hearthkeeper
description: You do not remember a hearth, but your hands remember tending one: how bread is judged, how a story about a neighbour keeps the neighbour. The Vale takes you for one of its own before you have said a word, and gives you Ansel's Ember to wear until you have earned a name that keeps itself warm.

name: Wayfarer
description: Your feet knew the road before your head knew anything. A Fernhold bow sits in your hand as if it had been cut for you; perhaps it was. The Woodfolk's custom is restraint, and you have the habit of taking only what you need, which is why you still have so little.

name: Reedborn
description: You swim as if you had been born in the water, and the Reedfolk say you were. You carry a jetty-lantern of the kind hung for the drowned, and you do not remember whose it was. Patience comes easily; so does the marsh's fatalism, which the Council will tell you is the same thing seen from a boat.

name: Cragborn
description: A bone ring on your finger says you crossed a chain bridge alone as a child, and no clan will say which one. The clans keep memory as a hand on the rope; you have lost yours, which to them is the saddest thing a person can be, and they will feed you for it.

name: Ashwalker
description: You wear grey without deciding to and count bells without meaning to. A Bell-Sworn signet was on your hand when the Warden found you at the Hushline, written at a Name-table by someone who came back from the Ash Winter. The Order does not ask questions; it has learned not to expect answers.

name: Lantern-Clerk
description: You read charters in your sleep and know what a signature costs. A factor's brass band says you once had standing in Tollmere; the Tallymen's ledger has no line for you now, and the Quiet Hands find that very interesting.
